subject: Initial packet/first-byte latency — streaming approach & pilot next steps
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@orchardhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: latency/streaming notes from this morning's discovery

Hi Samira — thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so our solutions/eng team can size a pilot: 

Summary from call:
- Goal: real-time clinical assistant in web EHR flows; low initial-latency experience is high priority.
- Preferred streaming method: browser-first (SSE) but some users will use mobile apps (possible fallback to WebSocket).
- Desired Pilot: subset of workflows (~3 templates), 2-week load/latency validation run.

Clarifying questions (to unblock a pilot SLO proposal):
1) TTFT target: you mentioned "sub-200ms feels right" — can you confirm a hard P95 or P99 target (e.g., P95 < 150ms)?
2) Concurrency & throughput: do you expect 100–200 concurrent users at peak, or should we plan for higher (burst to 400)? Any expected sustained RPS numbers?
3) Typical response size: average token count or expected characters per response (helps with chunk cadence recommendations).
4) Browser vs mobile: is SSE acceptable for mobile webviews, or do you need WebSocket for mobile clients?

Attach: I sketched an initial pilot runbook and a short playbook for SSE chunk cadence — I’ll attach the PDFs once we sync internally.

Next steps: if you confirm the short answers above, Ben and David will draft a short SLO proposal and a pilot MOP for your review by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@orchardhealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Orchard Health Technical Team <infra@orchardhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: latency/streaming notes from this morning's discovery

Thanks, Sofia — appreciate the summary. Answers inline below: 

1) TTFT target: Our clinical UX team wants a hard P95 of 120ms where feasible; P99 can be relaxed to 400ms for larger contexts. If a 120ms P95 is unrealistic we can accept P95 < 150ms as a fallback, but P95 120ms is the preference for the most latency-sensitive workflows.

2) Concurrency & throughput: Peak concurrent active sessions expected ~= 200 (clinic shift overlap). Sustained baseline ~30–50 RPS, with burst up to 120 RPS during batch check-ins. Please assume occasional spikes.

3) Response size: Typical responses are short (100–250 tokens) for quick clinical suggestions, but some templates will return longer summaries up to 600 tokens. For chunking: smaller quick chunks for the 100–250 token flows, fewer chunks for long summaries.

4) Browser vs mobile: SSE is preferred for web; for native mobile apps we may need WebSocket if the webview behavior is flaky. We can try SSE first and evaluate.

Security note: we will need the pilot to run in Redwood Dedicated or Private for PHI-sensitive flows — we flagged this with procurement.

Happy for you to proceed with the pilot proposal. Can you include an explicit fallback plan and a way to measure perceived latency (TTFT and first-render timing)?

—Samira
Samira Khan
Director, Platform Engineering | Orchard Health
samira.k@orchardhealth.com | +1 (617) 555-2642

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@orchardhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed pilot SLOs & streaming recommendations (draft)

Samira — excellent, that's very helpful. Ben and David and I discussed and put together a concise draft SLO + implementation notes below. Attached: sse-chunk-playbook.pdf (chunk cadence guidelines) and orchard-pilot-mop.pdf (pilot plan + success criteria).

Draft pilot SLOs (2-week run on Dedicated capacity):
- TTFT (first byte)
  - Target A (aggressive): P95 < 120ms, P99 < 400ms for short-response templates (~100–250 tokens).
  - Target B (practical): P95 < 150ms, P99 < 500ms across mixed templates (includes long-summary templates).
- End-to-end completion latency (useful for perceived performance): median end-to-end < 350ms for short templates.
- Availability: 99.9% for streaming connections during pilot window.

Throughput & concurrency assumptions to provision:
- Baseline RPS: 50
- Expected steady concurrency: 200
- Burst capacity: up to 400 concurrent connections; autoscale triggers at 250 concurrent.

Streaming recommendations (SSE-first):
- SSE preferred for browser clients; configure chunk cadence = 150–300ms for short responses (sends smaller first-chunk for immediate feedback).
- For long summaries (>400 tokens), batch 150–250 tokens per chunk with a cadence of 250–500ms to optimize cost.
- Heartbeat frame every 15s to keep connections alive behind proxies.
- WebSocket fallback: enable for mobile clients or environments where SSE drops frequently.

TTFT reduction techniques we will apply in pilot:
- Prefix/KV caching for common prompts/templates to avoid recompute on warm paths.
- Continuous batching with latency-aware windows tuned to keep P95 under target while maximizing throughput.
- Lightweight quantized model variant for ultra-low-latency flows (configurable per-template).

Measuring and instrumentation:
- We'll emit token-level first-byte timing (TTFT) and first-render timing to the console and to your tracing endpoint.
- Dashboard proposal: per-template P50/P95/P99 TTFT, concurrent connections, RPS, and chunk cadence histograms.

Next steps: Ben and David will draft the pilot MOP and an SLA appendix reflecting Target A and Target B. If you approve, we can spin up a Dedicated pilot cluster (private tenancy) and run the 2-week validation.

Attaching: sse-chunk-playbook.pdf (guidelines), orchard-pilot-mop.pdf (draft runbook).

Thanks —
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

- We'll target the aggressive TTFT in a canary group (Target A) and fall back to Target B if we see tail issues during the first 48 hours.
- Confirmed: pilot must run on Dedicated/Private for PHI. Please include estimated cost delta in the MOP.

Can you send the pilot MOP + SLA appendix to procurement and legal? I'll loop procurement once we have the DocuSign for the pilot statement of work.

If you can get DocuSign link in the next 24h we can aim to start the pilot the following week.
